course_name: Spring Cloud Gateway for a Strangler-Fig Migration to GKE
sequencing_rules: Respect every Requires edge in DESIGN (a node is only taught once all nodes it points to are already taught).
Prefer the order that reaches each DesiredResult fastest from the Baseline nodes, subject to that constraint.

Group topologically-tied nodes into a coherent narrative arc per session rather than strictly interleaving by minimal graph depth, when a session boundary or the 1-week gap between sessions makes that clearer for a mixed Dev/Ops room.
Keep every hands-on block offering a meaningful role to both personas (multi_lane) unless the underlying DESIGN node's audience/skippable_by/persona_variant restricts it to one persona.

design_decisions.summary: PRQ-LEGACY-TOKEN-FORMAT is a root node tagged [risk] in DESIGN: the legacy application's exact expected token shape is not in the specs and must be supplied by the client. It is scheduled briefly near the start of the token-minting block in Session 2; if the client has not supplied it by then, PRQ-TOKEN-MINTING-LOGIC, PRQ-TOKEN-PROPAGATION and DR-MINT-TOKEN cannot proceed as scheduled and this whole tail of Session 2 would need to fall back to a worked example instead of the team's real format.

The dev-only token-minting block at the end of Session 2 (custom filter authoring through DR-MINT-TOKEN, ~70 minutes) leaves both Ops participants in an observer role for a sustained stretch, which runs against the cross-persona design directive that every hands-on block give Ops a meaningful task. This is accepted because DR-MINT-TOKEN's audience is P-DEV only per DESIGN, but the trainer should actively use Ops's observer time (e.g. having them shadow-verify the resulting downstream request, or prep the capstone's operational checklist) rather than letting them disengage.

LOGISTICS states 2 sessions x 4h but does not itemize a setup/break buffer. This curriculum assumes 225 usable minutes per 240-minute session (a 15-minute buffer per session for Teams/remote friction, breaks, and questions) and budgets items against that figure. Confirm with the human whether 225 is the right usable-minutes figure before sign-off.

Strict quickest-path-per-node-depth would let DR-DEPLOY-GATEWAY, DR-VALIDATE-AUTH and DR-TRACING interleave more tightly since they sit at similar graph depth. Instead, DR-DEPLOY-GATEWAY and DR-STRANGLER-ROUTING (the two objectives already reachable once route config exists) are grouped into Session 1 as a 'get something running and split traffic' arc, and DR-VALIDATE-AUTH, DR-TRACING and DR-MINT-TOKEN are grouped into Session 2 as a 'secure, observe, extend' arc. This still respects every Requires edge; it optimizes for narrative coherence across the 1-week gap between sessions over strict depth-interleaving.

PRQ-K8S-DEPLOY-CONCEPTS is marked skippable_by P-OPS in DESIGN (Ops already hold this via BSL-GKE-CONTAINERS). It is kept as a short single_lane refresher for developers only rather than dropped entirely, since P-DEV's baseline does not include GKE comfort and PRQ-GKE-DEPLOY-GATEWAY depends on it.

items.title: End-to-end strangler-fig gateway capstone
items.rubric: Pass if, in one integrated run against the live GKE-deployed gateway: (1) the gateway is reachable, (2) /legacy/** and migrated paths split correctly, (3) a valid Entra JWT is accepted (an invalid one rejected) and CORS allows the approved origin, (4) a trace connects the gateway to a downstream/legacy call across the request, and (5) a downstream/legacy call carries a correctly-shaped minted token. Both participants jointly narrate and verify their part of the running system.
